title: lem:borel: Borel recovery of the first-chaos field l_N from u alone is only sketched, but prop:ctvar's well-definedness of F_N depends on it

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** `prop:decomp` Step (3); `lem:borel` ('Proof sketch'); `prop:ctvar` ('Borel measurability of the correct counterterm').

(q1-6, q1-7 were resolved for the *old* $B_\gamma$ construction; this is a distinct point in the current revision.)

The corrected observable is $F_N(u)=H_3(P_Nu;c_N)+3c_{N,2}\,\mathbf l_N(u)$. For this to be a genuine Borel functional **of $u$ alone**, one needs the map $u\mapsto \mathbf l_N(u)$ (the truncated **first-chaos / linear** component) to be Borel on a full-$\mu$ set $G$. This is asserted via `lem:borel` and a disintegration/measurable-selection argument given only as a sketch.

This is load-bearing and nontrivial: $\mathbf l$ is a *dynamic* object (the stationary linear solution), and recovering its fixed-time truncation $\mathbf l_N$ measurably from the single static distribution $u$ (not from the space-time noise) is exactly what makes `prop:ctvar`'s counterterm a function of $u$. The decomposition $u=\mathbf l-\mathbf C+v$ is not, a priori, uniquely determined by $u$ at a fixed time; uniqueness/measurability of the components must be established (e.g. via the regular conditional probability / measurable selection on the Polish space $\mathcal D'\times E$, with explicit verification that the selected $\mathbf l_N$ agrees $\mu$-a.s. with the dynamic one). Write out: (a) joint Borel measurability of $\Theta$, (b) $\nu(\mathcal G)=1$ with first marginal $\mu$, (c) the disintegration yielding $u\mapsto\mathbf l_N(u)$ Borel on $G$.
